recipes.name: Aubergine Curry
methods: Slice up the aubergines and tofu into cubes
Roast the aubergines in the oven for 25-30 minutes
Dice onions and garlic and saute until soft/translucent
Add the spices and mix
Add water to deglaze the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add peanut/almond butter and coconut milk and allow it to melt.
Add the aubergines and the cubed tofu into the pot and submerge
Cook for 10-15 minutes on a low heat.
Add soy sauce and brown sugar and combine.
Adjust flavours with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Baba Ganoush
methods: Cut aubergines in half
Cook the aubergines in the oven face down for 30 minutes
Take the aubergines from the oven and scoop the flesh out with a spoon into a bowl, discard the skin
Cut garlic cloves finely and juice the lemon
Add all ingredients into the bowl and combine with a fork
Using scissors, make rough cuts to the mix to reach your desired consistency. I like quite a fine texture but with still bits of aubergine for texture
notes: You can also use a blender to combine all the ingredients but I prefer to use scissors to have different textures in the dish

recipes.name: Banana Bread
methods: Mash the bananas in a bowl until mostly smooth.
Mix the mashed bananas with soy milk and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, combine oat flour, salt, baking powder, and bicarbonate.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Pour the batter into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350°F for 50-60 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: From Alex, modified from original source
Start with 1/4 cup soy milk and add more as needed for desired texture

recipes.name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chocolate Brownie
recipes.creator: Gaz Oakley
methods: Preheat oven to 180°C and line an 8×8 inch baking dish with parchment paper.
Cook sweet potato until tender by baking, boiling, or steaming. Combine with black beans, tahini, maple syrup, milk, and vanilla extract in a blender until smooth. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Fold in cacao powder, maca powder, Lions Mane, Chaga, sea salt, baking powder, hemp seeds, chia seeds, and chocolate chips.
Stir in olive oil and transfer batter to the lined tin. Top with chopped hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds.
Bake for 25-30 minutes.
Drizzle melted chocolate and sprinkle sea salt before serving.
notes: Store in the refrigerator for up to one week.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
methods: Combine half the onions (0.5 if using 1, so forth), ginger, coriander, garlic and chillies to a food processor for about 20 seconds.
Transfer mix to pot with cold/room temperature oil.
Bring pot to a medium heat for about 5 minutes.
In the meantime, add the tomatoes to a food processor for about 30 seconds
Add chilli powder, cumin, turmeric and fennel seeds to the pan and combine.
Add chickpeas and tomato blend to the pot.
Stir, lower the heat, close and let it cook for about 15 minutes
Add garam masala and salt at this stage.
Let it cook for another 8 minutes.
Cool down and serve with some rice, chapati or your carb of choice.
Garnish with coriander, diced onion and some green chillies.
notes: I use cashmere chilli powder if I have it.
I stem and seed the green chillies but adjust this to your desire level of heat.

recipes.name: Cilantro Scotch Bonnet Tempeh
methods: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Blend coriander, scotch bonnet, spring onions, garlic, preserved lemon, pomegranate molasses, sumac, soy sauce, olive oil, and sea salt until smooth.
Coat tempeh fillets in cornflour, then fry in oil until golden. Pour marinade over tempeh and cook until caramelized. Bake for 10 minutes.
Rehydrate porcini mushrooms in boiling water, then chop finely, reserving the liquid. Caramelize onions in olive oil, add mushrooms, white wine, mushroom liquid, beans, and salt. Simmer until creamy.
Serve tempeh with beans, garnished with coriander, pistachios, and reserved marinade.
recipes.creator: Gaz Oakley

recipes.name: Cilantro lime noodles
methods: Boil knife cut noodles according to package instructions and rinse with cold water. Keep some of the noodle water for later.
Combine chilli flakes with cilantro.
Heat up sesame oil and add to the mixture. You should observe sizzling when your pour the oil into the mix.
Add the rest of the ingredients and give it a good mix.
Pour over noodles, mix and top with toasted sesame seeds.
Serve as it is, or heat up gently in a pan
notes: I find knife-cut noodles perfect in this recipe but they can be hard to find

recipes.name: Creamy Vegetable Risotto

ingredients.name: warm vegetable stock, made with Marigold bouillon powder and water
asparagus or broccolini, trimmed and chopped
dry white wine, or extra vegetable stock
vegan parmesan, plus extra to serve

methods: Mix the bouillon powder into warm or boiling water, then keep the stock warm over a low heat.
Heat half the water or oil in a large pan. Add the asparagus or broccolini and red pepper, season, then cook for 3-4 minutes until just tender. Cover briefly to help them steam, then set aside.
Add the remaining water or oil to a wide pan. Cook the shallot over a medium heat for 1-2 minutes, until softened.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the wine or extra stock and cook until absorbed.

Add the warm stock one ladleful at a time. Stir often and keep the rice at a gentle simmer, adding more only as each ladleful is absorbed. Cook for 15-20 minutes, until creamy but still al dente. You may not need all the stock.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the vegan parmesan and most of the vegetables, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve straight away, topped with the remaining vegetables, extra vegan parmesan and parsley.
notes: Best eaten fresh. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for 2-3 days.
recipes.creator: Minimalist Baker

recipes.name: Lemon Cashew Pasta
methods: Soak the cashews in hot water for at least 10 minutes.
In a pan, sauté the onion until translucent, then add the garlic, parsley stems, and lemon zest and cook for a few more minutes.
Deglaze the pan with a splash of lemon juice to release all the flavors.
Blend the soaked cashews, veggie broth, nutritional yeast, and lemon juice in a blender or food processor to make the sauce
Pour the sauce back into the pan and add some parsley and/or basil.
Cook the pasta according to the packaging instructions until al dente, then save some pasta water
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce, mix well and add pasta water until it reaches your desired consistency.

recipes.name: Pasta with Pistachio Pesto
methods: (Optional) Toast the nuts until slightly browned from all sides for a deeper flavour.
Blend all ingredients for the pesto. Blend it as fine or coarse as you like.
Cook the pasta according to packaging instructions and save some of the pasta water.
Add the pesto to a large pan, add in the pasta and loosen with some pasta wate or oil.

recipes.name: Roasted Red Pepper and Cashew Pasta
methods: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Transfer the cashews to a bowl and cover in hot water straight from a kettle. Leave on one side to soak.
Remove the stem of the red peppers and cut the onion(s) in quarters.
Add the red peppers to a roasting tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Remove the tray from the oven. Add the quartered onions and garlic cloves and return to the oven for another 15 minutes.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water as per packet instructions and make sure you reserve some pasta water (1 cup for every 4 servings of this dish).
Leave the roasted veggies to cool for 5 minutes. Then peel the onion and garlic, and remove any skin and any remaining stalks or seeds from the red peppers. Transfer them to a blender.

Drain the cashews and add them to the blender, along with the plant-based milk and pasta water you reserved earlier, dried mixed herbs, sun-dried tomatoes (drain as much oil as possible), balsamic vinegar, nutritional yeast, and very generous pinches of salt and pepper
Blend until smooth.
Pour the sauce into a large saucepan on a low-medium heat. Gently heat the sauce, then add the spaghetti.
Top with basil, toasted cashews, and chilli flakes.
notes: If you don't have dried mixed herbs, use something like oregano or thyme

recipes.name: Red Lentil Dahl
methods: Dice onions and garlic and finely chop (or grate) ginger until you get paste
Combine all spices into a spice mix.
Put oil in a pot, once hot, add onions.
Once the onions have browned, add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant (add more oil if necessary). Stir and make sure the content of the pot does not stick to the bottom.
Add the spice mix into the pot and stir until combined. Again, try and prevent sticking to the bottom.
Add water to the pot and mix, make sure to scratch the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to avoid burning at the bottom.
Add the red lentils, tomatoes, and coconut milk to the pot.
Bring the mix to a boil and stir throughout.
Once boiling, bring down to a simmer, cover and let it cook for 15-20 minutes.
notes: DO NOT scale chilli flakes linearly with the servings scaling
I don't soak my red lentils but rinsing them can be a good idea
Keep stirring initially as onions have a tendency to stick to the bottom and might burn your whole dahl

recipes.name: Super Veggie
methods: Chop the cauliflower, broccoli, ginger, and garlic.
Boil the cauliflower, broccoli, ginger, garlic, and mushrooms together for 7-9 minutes until soft, then drain.
Add the cooked black lentils to a bowl as the base.
Top with your boiled veggies.
Finish with the cumin, hemp seeds, apple cider vinegar, and extra virgin olive oil.
recipes.creator: Bryan Johnson
notes: Bryan sometimes adds the juice of 1 lime and 1-4 tbsp of fermented foods (cabbage, kimchi, or beets).

Smoothie-bowl variant: add the boiled veggies, all other ingredients, and a little water to a blender and blend until smooth. Top with hemp seeds, extra virgin olive oil, and high-quality dark chocolate (optional).
One of Bryan's go-to longevity lunches — he eats it almost every day.

recipes.name: 1-Pan Tempeh Bolognese
methods: Heat a large-rimmed skillet, pot, or dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add oil and onion and sauté for 4-5 minutes until translucent and soft, stirring frequently.

Add mushrooms and stir. Sauté for 2 minutes more. Then add shredded tempeh and garlic. Add coconut aminos, fennel seeds, and red pepper flake. Sauté for 4-5 minutes until everything is golden brown, stirring frequently.
Add wine, stir, and cook for 1 minute. Then add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, vegan parmesan, and sweetener. Thin with water if needed. Stir to combine and simmer for 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust flavors as needed, adding more coconut aminos for saltiness, red pepper flake for spice, oregano for herbal flavor, tomato paste for depth, or vegan parmesan for cheesy flavor.
Serve with your favorite pasta or pasta alternative, like spaghetti squash or zucchini noodles, and garnish with fresh basil.
Cooled leftovers will keep covered in the refrigerator up to 5 days, or in the freezer up to 1 month. Reheat in a saucepan or microwave until hot, adding water as needed to rehydrate.
recipes.creator: Minimalist Baker

recipes.name: The Smoothest Hummus
methods: Boil some water with salt, add the chickpeas and garlic into the water, but keep the chickpea brine separate.
Boil the chickpeas for 20 to 30 minutes.
Drain the chickpeas once cooked and add to a blender with the chickpea brine and garlic clove from earlier.
Blend until they form a paste-like consistency.
Add in the tahini and blend, then whilst blending add in the ice cubes one at a time.
Add in the cumin, olive oil, salt, and lemon juice and blend one last time or until it's as smooth as desired.
Plate up the hummus, drizzle some olive oil over it and season with fresh parsley.

recipes.name: Vegan Thai Tom Yum Soup

ingredients.name: of soy sauce or vegan fish sauce
red chili paste/sauce (I use Sambal Oelek)

methods: With a pestle and mortar (ideally) crack lemongrass stalk
With a pesttle and mortar crush garlic and chiles
Prepare galangal, onions, tomatoes, mushrooms and baby corn
Heat a large pot over medium high heat, add oil and sauté onion and aromatics
Bring water to a boil in a separate pot and cook noodles to their specification, drain once they're ready
Add water and veg stock cubes to the pot and boil
Add mushrooms, baby corn, tomatoes, sugar, fish or soy sauce and salt to taste
Simmer for 5 minutes
Mix in lime juice, coconut milk and chili paste/sauce
Cook soup for another 7-8 minutes for flavors to infuse
(optional) Remove inedible aromatics (kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass)
Serve hot with more lime juice and cilantro if desired
notes: Fresh cilantro for garnish
Squeeze lime juice to squeeze for garnish
For the rice noodles I use the Udon Noodles by Yutaka (https://yutaka.london/products/noodles/udon-noodles-250g/)
If not using babycorn, feel free to replace babycorn for more mushrooms
I like to cook the soup and noodles separately to have the option to have the soup on its own or with noodles
